title: Skagit Health LTC Data Modernization Agent Huddle
setting: Monday morning, fictional Skagit Health Authority

agents.name: Elena Park
agents.role: Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent

agents.name: Owen Brooks
agents.role: Governance and Release BI Analyst Agent

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Good morning. I’m Maya Singh, Lead BI Analyst Agent and today’s huddle lead. The Project is open. We’ll decide what evidence supports, what stays blocked, and which tickets need human ownership. Daniel, you have the floor.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Thanks, Maya. I’m Daniel Cho, Analytics Director Agent. The first synthetic load lands cleanly; the second proves field mapping is insufficient. We found late Meditech corrections, repeated PARIS events, unmatched codes, and unresolved referral-note treatment. Skagit Health needs one Fabric foundation for many authorized workloads, without rebuilding nested views, manual steps, competing KPIs, weak monitoring, or limited lineage. Agents assemble evidence; accountable humans approve service levels, privacy rules, and release.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Clear. Inventory supports the decision, so I’m moving it to Done. Priya, take Meditech.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Priya Raman, Meditech Mapping BI Analyst Agent. I traced five corrected encounters. Latest modified timestamp selects current; discharge time cannot be the watermark. I’m blocking mapping and creating Capture late Meditech corrections for Human Data Engineering. I’ll attach evidence that Bronze retains both versions while one resolves current.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: Elena Park, Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent. I can package that evidence. Ha, a Monday victory for history.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Marcus Reed, PARIS Mapping BI Analyst Agent. Four rows are new deliveries of existing status events. Referral, status, and event time form the stable key; extract ID is lineage only. I’m blocking mapping and creating Define stable PARIS status-event keys for Human Data Engineering.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Marcus, I’ll compare key wording. At least the sources differ consistently.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: Elena Park, Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent. The ledger balances: 294 delivered rows become 279 current, nine duplicate or superseded, and six quarantined. Four lack identity links; two have an unmapped program. I’m starting reconciliation and creating Add reconciliation and quarantine outputs. Human Data Engineering gets reason codes; I can pair with the Human BI Analyst validating exceptions.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: Owen Brooks, Governance and Release BI Analyst Agent. Three gaps remain: referral-note security and privacy classification; correction, deletion, and retention treatment; and release validation requirements. I’m creating tickets for Human Privacy and Security, the Human Systems Owner, and the Human Analytics Director. We must support foreseeable authorized workloads.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Decision recorded: development continues; test promotion remains blocked. I’m starting common entities and creating Document cross-system matching exceptions for the LTC Source Mapping Working Group. A Human BI Analyst validates. Priya and Marcus provide evidence; Elena links reconciliation; Owen links approval gaps.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: That’s the right model. The Analytics Director Agent recommends and exposes evidence. The Human Analytics Director confirms criticality, product SLOs, and release. Human source owners confirm meaning. Privacy confirms treatment. A green check never means human approval.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Marcus, I can draft the exception table; you take PARIS rows.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Please do. I’ll annotate repeated events and unmapped programs. Ha, two awkward sources.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: I’ll add counts so a Human BI Analyst can reproduce exceptions.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: I’ll map rules to owners and gates. More red on this board is reassuring today.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Roll-up: two mapping tickets are Blocked, two foundation tickets are In Progress, and inventory is Done. Seven new tickets capture human work. I’m closing inventory; evidence stays in the repository.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We have thirty seconds. Any more questions, dependencies, or offers of help?

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: No question. Keep human approvals explicit in every ticket.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: No blocker beyond review. Marcus, I’ll send my draft today.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Works for me. I’ll return PARIS annotations before validation.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: I’ll keep reconciliation open and help either mapping stream.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: Nothing else. Release stays blocked until human decisions arrive.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Perfect. Decisions recorded, owners visible, help offered. Thank you. Happy Monday!

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Happy Monday!

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Happy Monday!

turns.text: Happy Monday!
